correctness.rationale: All 495^2=245025 restrictions were independently enumerated and row/column rank-reduced over two distinct exact prime fields: p=65581,t=62640 and p=65557,t=10574, with t primitive order 12 and p>4^8=65536. Both independently yield rank counts 0,1224,39384,204417 and 24 full-spark row sets. For any square minor k<=4 in Q(zeta12), Hadamard bounds each of four Galois conjugates by k^(k/2), so a nonzero algebraic norm is an integer of modulus at most k^(2k)<=65536. A vanishing mod-p evaluation would make the norm divisible by p, impossible if nonzero, hence every modular zero minor is exactly zero over C and conversely; modular rank equals complex rank. An independent orbit construction under r->ur+b (u unit mod12) yields exactly 21 row orbits covering all 495 row sets. Thus this is an exhaustive finite classification with an exact lifting theorem, not floating numerical rank or partial enumeration.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the complete rank incidence distribution and 21 affine profiles at the cyclic order-12 DFT. Previously published same-order full-spark classification gives the known 24 full-spark rows; this subclaim is not new. Earlier Delvaux–Van Barel works give structural rank-deficient block constructions and uncertainty relations, not the exact counts of all rank-2/3/4 four-by-four restrictions shown here. Different 15-/16-point rank censuses and the same-order 5-by-5 census do not imply the order-12 fourth-order distribution. Older exact unindexed tables remain possible.
residual_risks: Historical full-spark count 24 is known and is not asserted independently novel.
An old exact combinatorial rank table (not searched exhaustively) could imply some or all incidence values.
Finite-field exhaustiveness relies on the bounded algebraic norm argument; without it a modular rank would not certify complex rank.
